A genuinely new direction may still leave other null directions untouched, and a tiny component in the new direction need not produce a substantial smallest eigenvalue.

issues.failure_explanation: A subsampled gradient can produce an ascent direction for the full objective even when every Hessian is positive definite. For equally represented losses (theta-1)^2/2 and (theta+1)^2/2, a batch containing only the former at 0<theta<1 produces p=1-theta>0, while the full gradient is theta>0. No positive step along that direction decreases the convex full objective. Thus an ordinary full-objective descent line search cannot even accept a step, let alone supply the stated all-start convergence guarantee.
